stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in when the two species clean fish. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Marine biologist Tala Reyes studied two species of cleaner shrimp on a reef off the coast of Mindanao.
• The striped cleaner shrimp sets up its cleaning station on exposed coral heads.
• It services fish mostly during daylight hours.
• The pale cleaner shrimp sets up its cleaning station inside rock crevices.
• It services fish mostly after dusk.
• Both species remove parasites from more than a dozen species of reef fish.
choices: The striped cleaner shrimp services fish mostly during daylight hours, whereas the pale cleaner shrimp does most of its work after dusk.
While the striped cleaner shrimp works on exposed coral heads, the pale cleaner shrimp works hidden inside rock crevices.
Both the striped and the pale cleaner shrimp remove parasites from more than a dozen species of reef fish.
The pale cleaner shrimp, which sets up its cleaning station inside rock crevices, services fish mostly after dusk.
explanation: The goal limits you to one attribute: when the shrimp clean fish. Choice A names both species and sets their different times side by side (daylight versus after dusk), and 'whereas' states the contrast outright.

B.why: You found a real contrast between the two species, but it's about where they work, not when. The goal names timing, and this choice compares them on location.

C.why: You picked a sentence that mentions both species, but it describes something they share. The goal asks for a difference.

D.why: This gives the timing for only the pale cleaner shrimp. Without the striped shrimp's daylight schedule, there's nothing to contrast it with.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the drawbacks of speed humps and those of chicanes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Traffic planners use several tools to slow cars on residential streets.
• Speed humps are raised strips of pavement laid across the road.
• They are cheap to install.
• However, they can delay fire trucks by several seconds at each hump.
• Chicanes are curb extensions that force drivers to weave from side to side.
• They slow cars without jolting emergency vehicles.
• However, they take away on-street parking spaces.
choices: Speed humps are cheap to install, while chicanes slow cars without jolting emergency vehicles.
Speed humps can delay fire trucks at each hump, whereas chicanes take away on-street parking spaces.
Speed humps and chicanes are two of the tools planners use to slow cars on residential streets.
Speed humps are cheap to install but can delay fire trucks by several seconds at each hump.
explanation: The goal limits you to drawbacks. Choice B gives one drawback of each tool (delayed fire trucks, lost parking) and joins them with 'whereas,' so the difference between the two downsides is clear.

A.why: This compares the two tools, but on their advantages. You were asked about drawbacks, so a contrast between strengths doesn't do the job.

C.why: You chose a sentence that names both tools but never says how they differ, let alone how their drawbacks differ.

D.why: This covers only speed humps and even includes an advantage. Chicanes' drawback never appears, so no difference in drawbacks is shown.

stem: The student wants to emphasize how the two languages differ in the complexity of their tone systems. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Linguist Amara Osei documented two related languages, Kelu and Taro, spoken in neighboring valleys.
• Both languages use pitch to distinguish the meanings of words.
• Kelu has three contrasting tones.
• It has roughly 40,000 speakers.
• Taro has five contrasting tones.
• It has roughly 6,000 speakers.
choices: Kelu and Taro, which are spoken in neighboring valleys, both use pitch to distinguish the meanings of words.
With roughly 40,000 speakers, Kelu has far more speakers than Taro, which has roughly 6,000.
Kelu distinguishes word meanings using three contrasting tones, whereas Taro uses five.
Taro, which has roughly 6,000 speakers, distinguishes word meanings using five contrasting tones.
explanation: Here, the complexity of a tone system means how many tones it has. Choice C gives both counts, three for Kelu and five for Taro, and 'whereas' marks the difference.

A.why: This states a similarity. Both languages use pitch, but the goal asks how their tone systems differ.

B.why: You found a clear numerical contrast, but it's about how many people speak each language, not how complex the tone systems are. That's the wrong attribute.

D.why: This gives Taro's tone count but leaves out Kelu's, so there's nothing to compare it with.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in the ages of the two kilns. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Archaeologists have excavated two pottery kilns in the same river valley.
• The kiln at Dunmere has been radiocarbon dated to about 2400 BCE.
• It was used to fire plain cooking pots.
• The kiln at Hollin Ford has been radiocarbon dated to about 1900 BCE.
• It was used to fire decorated drinking cups.
• Both kilns were built from bricks of local clay.
choices: The Dunmere kiln fired plain cooking pots, whereas the Hollin Ford kiln fired decorated drinking cups.
Built around 1900 BCE, the Hollin Ford kiln was used to fire decorated drinking cups.
The Dunmere kiln, dated to about 2400 BCE, was built roughly five centuries after the Hollin Ford kiln.
The Dunmere kiln, dated to about 2400 BCE, was built roughly five centuries before the Hollin Ford kiln.
explanation: The goal is about age. Choice D names both kilns and states how far apart they are in time. A date of 2400 BCE is about 500 years earlier than 1900 BCE, so Dunmere came roughly five centuries before Hollin Ford.

A.why: This sets up a clear contrast, but it's about what each kiln produced, not how old each one is.

B.why: This gives only Hollin Ford's date. Without Dunmere's date, the reader can't see any age difference.

C.why: This reverses the order. BCE years count down toward year 1, so 2400 BCE is earlier than 1900 BCE, and Dunmere is the older kiln.

stem: The student wants to emphasize how the two coatings differ in durability. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Engineers tested two ceramic coatings designed to shield turbine blades from extreme heat.
• Each coating was heated and cooled repeatedly until it cracked.
• The zirconia coating cracked after about 1,200 heating cycles.
• The layered coating cracked after about 3,000 heating cycles.
• The zirconia coating is cheaper to produce.
• The layered coating insulates slightly less well than the zirconia coating does.
choices: The zirconia coating is cheaper to produce than the layered coating, which also insulates slightly less well.
The layered coating survived about 3,000 heating cycles before cracking, far more than the zirconia coating's 1,200.
Engineers heated and cooled both the zirconia coating and the layered coating repeatedly until each one cracked.
The layered coating insulates slightly less well than the zirconia coating but survived about 3,000 heating cycles.
explanation: Durability is measured by how many heating cycles a coating survives before cracking. Choice B gives both numbers and uses 'far more than' to spell out the difference.

A.why: This compares the coatings on cost and insulation. Neither one is durability, which is the attribute the goal names.

C.why: This describes the test method both coatings went through. It never reports a result, so it can't show a difference in durability.

D.why: This is the near-miss. It names both coatings, but the comparison it draws is about insulation. Only the layered coating's cycle count is given, so the durability difference is never stated.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in how the two types of fog form. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Fog forms when air near the ground cools to its dew point.
• Radiation fog forms on clear, calm nights as the ground loses heat.
• It usually burns off by midmorning.
• Advection fog forms when moist air moves over a cold surface, such as a chilly ocean current.
• It can persist for several days.
choices: Radiation fog forms as the ground loses heat on clear nights, while advection fog forms when moist air moves over a cold surface.
Radiation fog usually burns off by midmorning, whereas advection fog can persist along a coast for several days.
Radiation fog and advection fog are both types of fog, forming when air near the ground cools to its dew point.
Advection fog, which can persist for several days, forms when moist air moves over a cold surface such as an ocean current.
explanation: The goal narrows you to formation. Choice A gives the way each type forms, the ground losing heat versus moist air passing over a cold surface, and 'while' marks the contrast.

B.why: You found a real contrast, but it's about how long each fog lasts, not how it forms. That's the wrong attribute.

C.why: This names both types but describes what they have in common. The goal asks for a difference.

D.why: This explains how advection fog forms but says nothing about radiation fog, so there is no contrast.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the results of the two warm-up routines. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Sports scientist Lena Kowalczyk compared two warm-up routines in 48 collegiate sprinters.
• One group did static stretching for ten minutes before sprinting.
• The other group did dynamic drills, such as leg swings and skips, for ten minutes.
• Sprinters who did dynamic drills ran 40 meters an average of 0.08 seconds faster than those who stretched.
• The two groups reported similar muscle soreness the next day.
choices: One group of sprinters stretched in place before running, while the other group performed leg swings and skips.
Sprinters in both groups reported similar levels of muscle soreness on the day after their warm-ups.
Sprinters who did dynamic drills ran 40 meters about 0.08 seconds faster than those who did static stretching.
Dynamic drills, unlike static stretching, will make any athlete faster at every sprinting distance.
explanation: The goal asks about results, which is the finding stage of the study. Choice C gives the one result that differed between the groups, the 40-meter times, and names both routines in the comparison.

A.why: This contrasts the two routines themselves, which is the method. The goal asks how their results differed.

B.why: This is a result, but it's the one where the groups were alike. It shows a similarity, not a difference.

D.why: The study tested 48 collegiate sprinters over 40 meters. Claiming the effect holds for any athlete at every distance goes well beyond that evidence.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in how the two plant groups reproduced. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Paleobotanist Iris Nakamura studied plant fossils from a 300-million-year-old swamp deposit.
• Scale trees, a group of lycopsids, grew up to 30 meters tall.
• They reproduced by releasing spores.
• Seed ferns rarely exceeded 10 meters in height.
• They reproduced by producing seeds.
• Fossils of both groups are common in the deposit.
choices: Scale trees grew up to 30 meters tall, while seed ferns rarely exceeded 10 meters in height.
Fossils of both scale trees and seed ferns are common in the 300-million-year-old swamp deposit.
Seed ferns, which rarely exceeded 10 meters in height, reproduced by producing seeds.
Scale trees reproduced by releasing spores, whereas seed ferns reproduced by producing seeds.
explanation: The goal limits you to reproduction. Choice D gives each group's method, spores versus seeds, and 'whereas' states the difference.

A.why: This is a clear contrast, but it's about height, not reproduction. The goal names a specific attribute, and this compares the groups on a different one.

B.why: This names both groups but only says their fossils are common in the deposit. That's a shared feature, not a difference.

C.why: This gives how seed ferns reproduced but not scale trees, so there's nothing to compare it with.
